reason: C2 is a supply/clock-domain decoupling or feedthrough capacitor (VDD to net44); removing it usually preserves the DC and logical regeneration behavior, mainly affecting noise immunity and transient kickback.
impact_estimate: Low (more supply/clock feedthrough and possibly higher metastability/noise sensitivity).

reason: C1 (net66 to net72) behaves like a dynamic coupling/bootstrapping capacitor between a clocked node and a bias/load node; deleting it typically keeps the core latch/differential path functional but reduces dynamic gain/speed shaping.
impact_estimate: Low-to-moderate (slower or less decisive regeneration; changes in kickback/charge-sharing).

reason: C0 (net14 to net82) is another coupling/charge-sharing capacitor tied to a clocked/bias node; removing it mainly changes edge behavior and internal node slewing without breaking the main switching path.
impact_estimate: Low-to-moderate (timing and dynamic offset may shift; increased sensitivity to clock skew).
